projects.name: Wiredove
projects.tagline: A social application you can make your own.
projects.blurb: Wiredove brings profiles, posts, replies, and shared media into a browser application built on ANProto. You hold the keys to your identity and can back them up for use in another browser.
projects.update: Wiredove and this website’s timeline now use the same shared application. Improvements to publishing, profiles, and media can reach both through coordinated releases.
projects.next: Proposed: readable web pages for individual posts, so shared links open the conversation and show useful previews wherever they travel.
projects.screenshotNote: Earlier interface, archived August 2026. A fresh live capture is pending.

projects.name: ANProto
projects.tagline: Signed messages. Bring your own network.
projects.blurb: ANProto is the small protocol underneath Wiredove: a signature over a timestamp and a content hash. It establishes verifiable authorship without deciding how a message must travel.
projects.update: Implementations exist in JavaScript, Go, Rust, and Python. Wiredove and this site’s timeline put the protocol into everyday use; further experiments explore shared work between people and agents.

projects.name: Secure Scuttlebot Classic
projects.tagline: Keeping a peer-to-peer social network working.
projects.blurb: Secure Scuttlebot Classic continues the classic Scuttlebutt model on a modern Node.js stack: signed personal feeds, messages replicated between peers, private conversations, and shared files.
projects.update: It includes Decent, a browser client with several interchangeable appearances, and Git over SSB, which lets the network carry software repositories. I use that capability to maintain copies of these projects alongside GitHub.
projects.credit: Built on the contributions of Dominic Tarr, Paul Frazee, Charles Lehner, and the wider Scuttlebutt community. My work on Decent began in 2016.

projects.name: evbogue.com
projects.tagline: A personal website that participates in the work.
projects.blurb: This site holds my writing, recovered archive, and an interactive timeline powered by the shared Wiredove application. It is also where I use what I build.
projects.update: Recent work connected the timeline to the shared application, restored support for large historical photographs, and checked recovery of the available media. Maintaining a personal site makes the questions concrete: can the work still be read, and can it be recovered?

projects.name: Bogbook
projects.blurb: Four years building my own protocol from scratch, getting it wrong three times on purpose — no replication strategy, then an append-only log, then a backward hash chain that finally synced fast. The laboratory that became ANProto once every load-bearing piece had been removed. A terrible name for marketing materials.

projects.name: Far Beyond The Stars
projects.blurb: The minimalism blog I wrote when blogs still felt like they could change your life. I lived out of a bag, wrote every day, and grew an audience without a publisher, a platform deal, or anyone's permission. Most of that work is recovered and living in the archive here.
